resources.string: Your phone is the wheel. Your PC is the car.
Open Slipstream Hub on the PC and scan its QR code, or type the code it shows.
Key fingerprint %1$s. The code never leaves this phone.
Looking for Slipstream Hub on this network. Start the hub on the PC; phone and PC must share the Wi-Fi, the phone\'s hotspot or USB tethering.
UDP over the local network. Best on 5 GHz or the phone\'s own hotspot.
About 1 ms and lossless. Needs USB debugging on; the hub sets up adb reverse.
Recommended. The same packet on both paths; the first to arrive wins.
The phone pairs with Windows as a game controller. No hub needed.
Bluetooth gamepad: pairing happens in Windows Bluetooth settings.
Waiting for the hub to appear on the network, or scan its QR code.
Over the USB cable through adb reverse.
No hub seen on Wi-Fi yet: USB only, and Wi-Fi joins as soon as the hub appears.
Type the 16 character code shown by Slipstream Hub. Dashes and spaces are optional.
That is not a valid code. It has 16 characters from A to Z and 2 to 7.
Saved. This code does not match %1$s, so it will not connect to that hub.
Point the camera at the QR code in Slipstream Hub
That QR code is not a Slipstream pairing code.
This phone does not offer the Bluetooth HID device profile (Android 9 or later, and some makers disable it). Use Wi-Fi or USB instead.
Bluetooth permission is needed to act as a gamepad. If it was refused for good, allow Nearby devices in the app settings.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and the gamepad starts by itself.
Ready. On the PC open Settings, Bluetooth and devices, Add device, and pick Slipstream Wheel.
